correctness.rationale: The nonzero endemic polynomial has degree M. Every attracting interior root, including a degenerate one, has left-positive and right-negative field, so k attractors require at least 2k−1 distinct roots. The proposed quotient is polynomial since its numerator vanishes at 1. Each normalized coefficient is an alternating initial sum of elementary symmetric functions, strictly positive since the sum of the nonconstant elementary symmetric functions is bounded by the finite geometric sum of 2^−s. Multiplication recovers −yR(y)/R(1) for recovery 1 (and positive scaling supplies arbitrary recovery). The derivative at each root has the claimed alternating sign. The interval boundaries and exclusion of y=0 from the count are consistent. Rational refers to the formula in the roots, with rational coefficients for rational root data. The minimum largest group size is 2k. Independent exact replay `python3 /workspace/branches/independent-replay.py 3` checked 16 root prescriptions by exact polynomial division and reproduced the five-rate witness and normalization; the proof, not these sample cases, supplies the all-order conclusion.
residual_risks: Only the scalar deterministic mean-field family is established; no stochastic or hydrodynamic extension is implied.

value.rationale: Considered as a mathematical fact separately from credit for originality, an all-order exact stable-attractor capacity in a recognized mean-field model is useful. The degree count only supplies a ceiling; simultaneous strict coefficient positivity is a meaningful realization constraint. The extremal result gives an exact order requirement rather than a finite list of bifurcation cases.
residual_risks: The result has deterministic model-level significance only; novelty of this record is assessed separately.
